text:
Connor McDavid has a point in all 19 games to start the season, NHL.com noted after Monday's 3-1 win over the Rangers, and that streak is the clearest picture of where Edmonton is: 13-3-3, 29 points, a 96 percent chance at the playoffs in our simulations and a projection of about 105 points.

The engine is the obvious one. McDavid, Leon Draisaitl and Vasily Podkolzin have taken 62 percent of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) in their minutes together and outscored opponents 20-6. Mattias Ekholm and Evan Bouchard are 20-4 as a pair.

Here's the worry. As a team the Oilers take 51.7 percent of expected goals overall and 49 percent at five on five, which is the profile of a decent team, not a dominant one. They've scored 77 goals on 56.58 expected, 20 more than the chances suggest, and our numbers say they have about seven more points than their play has earned. Away from the top line it gets thin: Mathieu Joseph, Alex Formenton and Owen Michaels have only 33 percent of the expected goals together.

What to watch: whether the depth holds while Isaac Howard is on injured reserve (per the club's release), and Jake Walman, a healthy scratch for the fifth time in seven games according to Oilersnation. Devon Levi stealing Monday's game helped. Finishing at this rate won't last; the top line has to keep carrying it when it cools.
headline: McDavid's streak, and a team running ahead of itself
